limitations: The exact transaction is canonical and the negotiation path is preserved in a stored history distilled from the contemporary WhatsApp export, but Robert's original numeric decision state has not yet been reconstructed.
The currently available evidence preserves Robert's offer and Tim's acceptance, but not a complete contemporaneous statement of Robert's own roster thesis, hard price ceiling or protected assets.
Later 2025/2026 player outcomes for Jaxson Dart and Harold Fannin are excluded from this ex-ante reconstruction.

evidence_basis.note: Confirms the completed one-for-one TeamID 1 ↔ TeamID 6 trade: Robert received Jaxson Dart and Tim received Harold Fannin.

Distilled from the contemporary WhatsApp export: Robert asked about Dart on Tim's bench and directly offered Fannin. Robert framed Fannin as youth for Tim's older TE group / Njoku situation. Tim accepted immediately without asking for an add-on and said his QB depth made Dart expendable.
The 2025 league configuration had two dedicated QB starter slots.
Robert acquired Harold Fannin via waiver on 2025-09-10, about six weeks before the trade.
Tim selected Jaxson Dart at 2025 Rookie 4.03 (overall pick 21).

decision_context.objective: Acquire Jaxson Dart from Tim's QB surplus in a two-QB dynasty league by offering Harold Fannin in a direct one-for-one trade.
decision_context.roster_context: The league required two starting quarterbacks. The currently preserved contemporary evidence does not yet fully reconstruct Robert's own QB-room need, but it does show that Tim viewed Dart as expendable because of his existing QB depth.
decision_context.cap_salary_context: No salary/cap rationale is preserved for this 2025 trade and none is used in the reconstruction.
decision_context.team_window: The transaction involved two young 2025 rookies and appears oriented toward multi-year dynasty roster construction rather than a short-term veteran rental.
decision_context.market_context: Robert identified Dart as an available bench asset on a roster with QB surplus and offered a young TE who fit Tim's thinner/older TE context. Tim accepted the one-for-one offer immediately without seeking an add-on.
decision_context.why_now: Dart was available on Tim's bench, while Fannin had been acquired by Robert on waivers several weeks earlier and could be used as a direct roster-fit bridge.
constraints: The exact hard ceiling Robert would have paid for Dart is not yet reconstructed.
The exact degree to which Robert viewed Fannin as expendable versus valuable upside is not yet reconstructed.
No add-on was required; Tim accepted the initial one-for-one offer.

theses.statement: In a two-QB dynasty format, converting Harold Fannin into young quarterback upside through Jaxson Dart could improve long-term roster optionality.
falsification_conditions: Robert did not materially value additional young-QB optionality at the time.
Fannin's expected dynasty value was already high enough that Robert viewed the one-for-one exchange as poor value.

theses.statement: The trade exploited a roster-fit asymmetry: Tim considered Dart surplus at QB, while Robert could offer a young TE who fit Tim's older TE/Njoku situation.
falsification_conditions: Tim did not actually view Dart as expendable because of QB depth.
Fannin did not materially improve the roster area Robert was using to make the offer attractive to Tim.

alternatives.description: Keep Harold Fannin and do not acquire Jaxson Dart.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert proactively approached Tim about Dart and preferred completing the one-for-one exchange.

price_ceiling.description: The final trade was Fannin for Dart one-for-one and Tim accepted the initial offer immediately. Robert's hard maximum price for Dart is not yet reconstructed.

known_risks.description: Fannin was a young TE asset whose development/value trajectory was still uncertain, so moving him could sacrifice meaningful TE upside.
Dart was also a rookie developmental asset, so the added quarterback optionality carried substantial player-outcome uncertainty.
Tim's immediate acceptance created a negotiation-process risk that Robert may have offered more than necessary or could potentially have sought an add-on.

decision_state_at_execution.confidence_rationale: The transaction and contemporary negotiation path are well supported, but Robert's subjective confidence level has not yet been reconstructed.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_confidence_driver: The observable strategy was to target a young QB from Tim's surplus and use Fannin as a roster-fit bridge in a two-QB league.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_source_of_doubt: Robert's contemporaneous view of Fannin's upside, Dart's probability of becoming a useful starter and whether the immediate one-for-one price felt cheap/fair/expensive remain to be reconstructed.
